signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 189.10, showing pronounced cross underperformance as the G10 Currency Strength Scorecard flags a critical 1.645% leader-to-laggard divergence. JPY leads the G10 complex with an average weekly gain of +0.946% across 7 pairs, while CHF lags at -0.699% across 6 pairs. While the nominal policy spread gives SNB 0.00% vs BoJ 1.25% with a 125bp carry favor to JPY, Iran Strait of Hormuz closure headlines inject fresh geopolitical friction into energy routes, compounding the move. Options markets reflect intense hedging demand for JPY strength, with EUR/JPY 25d risk reversals printing at -2.50. BEER valuation also flags CHF/JPY as structurally cheap at z=-1.96 standard deviations below model fair value of 196.02, though momentum remains dictated by bilateral flows. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY, tracking G10 bilateral divergence. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions release. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Middle East relieve pressure on European currencies and arrest the JPY advance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.34, holding above its SMA20 of 156.28 while remaining capped beneath the SMA50/200 cluster at 158.49/158.45. A substantial 275bp policy differential favors USD with Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%, matched by a +267bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry cushion. However, the options market exhibits a severe divergence: 1M 25d risk reversals sit at -2.57, marking an extreme put skew that indicates heavy institutional demand for downside protection despite positive carry. Concurrently, USD/JPY 1M implied vol at 9.1% trades below 30-day realized vol of 10.1%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of -1.1% that signals options market pricing compression. Positioning data shows leveraged funds net long JPY at +4,472 contracts, sitting in the 98th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +2.66 despite a weekly reduction of 15,597 contracts. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY on downside hedging demand. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI and BoJ Tankan survey release. Risk: Break and daily close above the SMA50 resistance at 158.49 restores the carry-led grind toward 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Stretched Speculative Short + Rate Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1374, pinned beneath its daily SMA20 at 1.1526, SMA50 at 1.1538, and SMA200 at 1.1623. A 135bp rate spread favors USD with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%, reinforced by a +146bp SOFR-€STR OIS basis. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds short EUR at -58,805 contracts, falling in the 19th percentile of the 52-week distribution (z=-1.01) after an outflow of 7,450 contracts WoW. However, eurozone macro data presents an active divergence against technical weakness: the Economic Surprise Index for the euro stands at +18.2 with 170 beats against 107 misses, reflecting resilient underlying economic prints. With 1M 25d risk reversals printing at a mild put skew of -0.50, options participants refrain from aggressive downside positioning despite spot testing summer lows. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish EUR/USD, constrained by positive carry for the dollar. Catalyst: Euro Area Consumer Price Expectations and Lagarde speech. Risk: Stronger German and French inflation prints force an upward repricing of the ECB rate trajectory.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Institutional vs Retail Positioning Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD sits at 0.5663, trading well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5777, 0.5840, and 0.5853 following five consecutive weeks of losses. A wide 125bp policy rate differential favors USD with Fed at 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75%, backed by a 115bp SOFR-overnight OCR spread. An extreme positioning divergence has developed between participants: retail sentiment is 91% long, representing an extreme contrarian crowding into a downtrend. In contrast, institutional leveraged funds remain net short -5,216 contracts following an additional 2,897 contracts trimmed WoW. BEER valuation indicates NZD/USD is statistically stretched to the downside at z=-1.57 standard deviations below model fair value of 0.5781, creating an asymmetric risk profile if retail accounts are forced to liquidate. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, contrarian to retail extreme long positioning. Catalyst: United States Core PCE Price Index release. Risk: RBNZ rate expectations accelerate further, triggering a sharp short squeeze toward 0.5750.
